<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cfcba539205a2b11e363168ccc2647e74addac0d`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cfcba539205a2b11e363168ccc2647e74addac0d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4da3544c5261d5ecd877a60daeda0bf2d6ff6f6` — the merge of head `18533305469c6cb51551b62f6c2b14cf6ea5d939` into base `cfcba539205a2b11e363168ccc2647e74addac0d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4da3544c5261d5ecd877a60daeda0bf2d6ff6f6 && git checkout d4da3544c5261d5ecd877a60daeda0bf2d6ff6f6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cfcba539205a2b11e363168ccc2647e74addac0d 18533305469c6cb51551b62f6c2b14cf6ea5d939 && git checkout -B drift-repro cfcba539205a2b11e363168ccc2647e74addac0d && git merge --no-ff 18533305469c6cb51551b62f6c2b14cf6ea5d939

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cfcba539205a2b11e363168ccc2647e74addac0d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cfcba539205a2b11e363168ccc2647e74addac0d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `07a5f786ce8ee8da1fe3e3268690b3848848266e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/objectql/src/disabled-holder-packageless-row-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts (cited code, read on main, never reviewed); .changeset/34144-bare-save-holder-judgment.md judged for ② only
Security-touching: no

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Read: the three cards with every comment, the PR body, file list, comments and net diff against `main`, the 51 check-runs on this head, AGENTS.md and ADR-0150 on `main`, and the cited code. Nothing was built or run; every judgment below is a reading of the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff adds one judgment, `packagelessHolderRefusal`, at three call sites, each placed after the existing refusals. It only returns a refusal or `undefined`, so no answer that was refused becomes accepted. RIGHT.

Moved, accepted to refused, as the tree reads:

- Two or more enabled holders, publish save, over no row or over one package's row: 200 to `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming the enabled holders. RIGHT; it is the resolver's own refusal (`resolveItem` naming no package), the call the bare read makes in `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`.
- Same state, draft save (`?mode=draft`): 200 to 409 naming them. RIGHT.
- Same state, bare delete over one package's row: removed to 409 naming them, row stays. RIGHT.
- Every holder disabled, publish save over the disabled package's row, over no row, and at a bundled member the holder never ships (#34262): 200 to 409 with the `?package=` remedy, naming no package. RIGHT; the message is built from the verb, type and name alone.
- Same state, draft save and bare delete over the disabled package's row: 200 to 409 naming none. RIGHT.
- Row bound to a customization pair of a disabled holder: counted as that holder, as the read face's `isHoldersPairRow` withholds it. RIGHT.

Not moved, confirmed by reading:

- A write naming a package: every call site is guarded on no package named.
- The environment's own item (`getEnvironmentScopedItem`) and a package-unbound row at the address (`address.unbound`).
- One enabled holder; a name no package holds.
- A row bound to an id no installed package has: `isPackageDisabled` reads it as enabled, so the later named-base refusal still answers.
- The #32605 cells on the publish save: `servedPackagelessSaveAddress` answers first.
- Server-stated rewrites (`source` set) and `package-duplicate`.

Named WRONG or incomplete:

- The changeset says the bare delete "used to remove the one package's row". The same call also moves the bare delete and the bare draft discard over NO stored row. That path answered `success: true, reset: false` (the no-op receipt, after the registry self-heal) and now answers 409 in both states. Undeclared and unpinned: S2.
- "Every moved answer goes from accepted to refused" is not the whole motion. A bare save in these two states that a later gate refused (an invalid body, a read-only inherited package) now answers this 409 first. Still refused, and the same rank as the existing two-bindings refusal: nit N4.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`. AGENTS.md Post-Task 3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition. Correct.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: no key, accepted value or metadata type changes; the same item is still writable by naming its package. Correct.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: line-initial in the PR body and the changeset, a legal pairing, BREAKING. The BREAKING banner is in both.
- `!`: on the PR title and the changeset summary line.
- ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The reason holds: no schema key, export or stored row changes.
- `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (a package-unbound row of a name only disabled packages ship: bare read 404, bare save 200 and hidden): ESCALATED, not answered. Ruling A's remedy does not reach a package-unbound row, and the cell is a read/write asymmetry the ruling's wording arguably covers. It needs the maintainer's word: S3.
- Dev acceptance note (two enabled holders plus a package-unbound row: bare read 409, bare save edits the row): the same class, escalated in the same card: S3.
- Dev flag "dogfood battery owed again on the final head": the dev's reading is at `6401aad2f3` and no later report is on the cards. On this head the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` context is success; PR runs skip the shards and the queue run adds them (AGENTS.md, two speeds). The PR's own source hunks are unchanged since the measured head. Answered: the queue run carries it.
- Dev deviations (pins added to the shared #32605 harness, `put` gained a query argument; unpushed amend before the first push): accepted, no contract effect.
- Out-of-scope carrier #33995: resolved on this head. #33995 is merged, `main` is merged in, and the S3 save pin is flipped with its delete half and shipped-member CONTROL kept.
- All 51 check-runs on this head: success or skipped, none failed.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The one new store read is `packagelessAddress` at `active` on the draft path, a `WHERE type, name, state` read. The unions are over holder ids from the in-memory registry; no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. ADR-0150 D5 on `main`: a bare address resolves while the name has one holder and answers 409 otherwise, "never a silent pick", with no new code minted. D3: a caller with no package gets the environment's item first, else the unique holder, else the refusal. The save and delete now give that answer through the read's own resolver call, with the existing `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. The disabled-only arm rests on ruling A on #34144 and the registry's served-holder rule (#32183), not on ADR text: N3.

Does the write door count holders as the bare read does, cell by cell:

- Environment's own item: yes, the same `getEnvironmentScopedItem` test; left alone.
- `?package=` writes: not judged, unchanged.
- Single enabled holder: yes, the resolver resolves and the disabled-only test finds an enabled id.
- Two or more enabled holders, no disabled binding among the rows: yes, on publish save, draft save and delete.
- Mixed, publish save, one enabled and one disabled holder: yes, by #32605's step, untouched.
- Mixed, publish save, two enabled holders and a disabled binding among the rows: NO in one sub-cell, S1.
- Mixed, draft save and delete: NO, unchanged from `main`. Neither door has the #32605 step, so both take the address from the rows: the disabled holder's row is written or removed while the read serves the enabled holder. Over a row of each, the delete's 409 names the disabled package. Folded into S1's follow-up.
- Types the registry does not read by package (`action`, `doc`, whose bare reads refuse through their own judges): not judged here. The PR body says so; the changeset's "Not moved" list does not: N4.

Leak check on the disabled-only refusal: it names no package. `disabledHoldersOnlyRefusal` takes only the verb, the shown type and the name; the delete rethrows it as it is. It does disclose that some disabled package holds the name (409 where a free name saves), which is inherent to ruling A.

S1 (should-fix) — one cell of #33955 survives on the publish save, by reading. State: two enabled packages E and F hold the name, and the stored rows are bound to a disabled package and to exactly one enabled package (E). `servedPackagelessSaveAddress` reads no served address, sees the disabled binding, keeps the one enabled binding and returns E. The new judgment sits in the other branch and is never asked. The save writes E's row (200); the bare read refuses 409 naming E and F. Unchanged from `main` and outside the cards' measured states, so not a regression. Either ask the resolver arm before the enabled-bindings pick, or file the follow-up card with the mixed delete and draft cells before `Fixes #33955` closes the card. Until then the helper's jsdoc ("answer the name as the bare read does") overclaims.

S2 (should-fix) — declare and pin the no-row delete. A bare delete or bare draft discard over no stored row moves from the no-op success receipt to 409 in both states. Add the FROM-TO to the changeset and one pin per state, or guard the delete call on a row being addressed.

S3 (should-fix) — file the decision card for the package-unbound-row cells (③): beside a disabled-only name (read 404, save 200 hidden) and beside two enabled holders (read 409, save 200).

- N1 (nit): the new catch uses `instanceof PackageScopedNameRefusedError` alone. The package's own recogniser `packageScopedRefusalOf` also reads the shape across a copied class. A copy would rethrow the resolver's 409 without the save remedy; still refused.
- N2 (nit): the disabled-only delete pins assert code and status only, not the `?package=` remedy or that no package is named. Delete pins go through the protocol, not the two transports.
- N3 (nit): the changeset cites ADR-0150 D3 for "a disabled package holds no name". ADR-0150 on `main` has no such sentence; the authority is ruling A and the registry rule of #32183.
- N4 (nit): two changeset wordings. "Still refused `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`" for a shipped member holds only where the package door refuses; in the runtime harness that save moved 200 to 409. The "Not moved" list omits the types not read by package and the refused-to-refused code moves in ①.
- N5 (nit): the draft path reads the active rows for every bare draft save before asking whether the type is read by package. The PR is still marked draft and its body still carries the "Waits on #33995" banner, stale at this head.

No must-fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e378b62f30969c2b0466666b8572af1d686f6aec`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/objectql/src/disabled-holder-packageless-row-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (cited code, read on main and at this head, never reviewed); .changeset/34144-bare-save-holder-judgment.md judged for ② only
Security-touching: no

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). This is the delta record after PASS 6911434197 at `07a5f786ce8ee8da1fe3e3268690b3848848266e`. Read: the three cards with every comment, follow-up cards #34346 and #34348, the PR body, file list, comments, the net diff against `main`, the round's delta `07a5f786..e378b62f`, the 51 check-runs on this head, AGENTS.md and ADR-0150 on `main`, and the cited code. Nothing was built or run; every judgment is a reading of the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

The round's delta is four commits over four files. By reading, no answer moves relative to `07a5f786`:

- `protocol-save.ts`: the resolver catch in `packagelessHolderRefusal` now reads the refusal through `packageScopedRefusalOf` (the read's own recogniser, exported from `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`) in place of `instanceof` alone. Same answer for the class instance. A copied class of the same shape is now recognised and restated as the write's refusal, where before it was rethrown as the resolver's 409: refused to refused. Anything else is still rethrown. RIGHT.
- `protocol-save.ts` and `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`: otherwise jsdoc and comments only. The two "Known gap" paragraphs name the surviving mixed cells, and the helper's claim is narrowed to "in the two states below".
- Test file: two new pins and one firmer assertion helper. No harness behaviour changes.
- Changeset: wording only (②).

The moved answers of the whole PR, as the tree reads on this head, are the earlier record's list plus the one it found undeclared, now declared:

- A bare delete or bare draft discard over NO stored row, in both states: the no-op receipt (`success: true, reset: false`) to `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Two enabled holders: naming both. Only disabled holders: the `?package=` remedy, naming none. RIGHT. The delete call site asks the judgment whenever no package is named, before the row probe, and the changeset and the PR table now say so.

Not moved, re-confirmed on this head:

- Every call site is still guarded on no package named.
- `address.unbound` and `getEnvironmentScopedItem` still return before either arm.
- A delete naming the package over no row is still the no-op receipt (pinned as CONTROL in both new pins).

`main` has not touched `protocol-save.ts`, `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` or `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` since the merge base `66f6638fa4`, so the base brings no semantic drift into these doors.

### ② Semver level

- Level `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-initial in PR body and changeset, `!` on title and summary, BREAKING banner in both, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: unchanged and still correct (AGENTS.md Post-Task 3).
- The changeset now declares the no-row delete and draft discard FROM-TO in both states.
- It cites ruling A and the registry's served-holder rule (#32183) for "a disabled package holds no name", not ADR text.
- It qualifies the `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` line ("where the package door refuses it").
- It lists the types not read by package and the save's refused-to-refused move under "Not moved".
- It states that it supersedes the "accepted and kept, as before" line of `.changeset/33385-disabled-holders-env-404.md` (line 19 on `main`, left unedited): N8.
- `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `PR-body guards` are success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Earlier escalation (package-unbound row beside a disabled-only name, and beside two enabled holders): carried by decision card #34348, open, labelled `needs-user-decision`, both cells named with options. Answered by the card; not this PR's scope.
- Hand-off flag "commits after `07a5f786` pushed before their local run; S2 ablation never run": on this head `Test Core` (8 shards), `Type Check · workspace`, `Build Core` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are success, which is the reading for the TO side of the new pins. The FROM side (the no-op receipt) is read from the tree, not ablated: N7.
- Hand-off flag "overlap with #34238 in `protocol-save.ts`": not on `main` at this base; `mergeable_state` is clean. The second to land reconciles, as the takeover claim records. No finding here.
- Hand-off flag "contradicting unreleased changeset": answered in this PR's changeset by the supersede sentence. See N8.
- Hand-off flag "a delta `os-dev-report` on #34144 is owed": none is on the card. The PR body's Verification section states what was and was not measured. Process item for the seat, no contract effect.
- All 51 check-runs on this head: success or skipped, none failed or pending.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The delta adds no store read; the PR's one new read is still the `WHERE type, name, state` read of the active rows on the draft path.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing still makes the spec's own refusal real and takes no declared capability away. ADR-0150 D5 on `main`: an ambiguous bare address answers 409, "never a silent pick", with no new code. D3: the environment's item first, else the unique holder, else the refusal. Refusing the no-row delete and draft discard is consistent with that: over no row the address is as ambiguous (two enabled holders) or as unheld (only disabled holders) as it is for the save, and the write named by `?package=` still answers the receipt. The disabled-only refusal still takes only the verb, the shown type and the name, so it names no package; the new helper `expectDeleteRefusedNamingNone` now pins that on the delete.

Earlier items against this head:

- S1: the cell is unchanged in the tree, as declared. Follow-up card #34346 is filed (open, p2, queue) and carries the publish save, the draft save and the delete, with acceptance on the two-enabled-plus-disabled-binding state, CONTROLs and the narrowing declaration. Both helpers' jsdoc now names the gap and no longer overclaims. See N6 for one cell its acceptance does not list.
- S2: declared in the changeset for both states, in the PR table, and pinned once per state (`d_norow_dash`, `two_norow_dash`), delete and draft discard, with the package-named receipt as CONTROL and no row stored afterwards.
- S3: decision card #34348 is filed and carries both cells.
- N1: the catch uses `packageScopedRefusalOf`.
- N2: the disabled-only delete pins assert the `?package=` remedy and that neither package id is named. They still go through the protocol, not the two transports; accepted.
- N3: the changeset cites ruling A and #32183.
- N4: both wordings corrected.
- N5: the stale wait banner is gone. The PR is still marked draft, and the draft path still reads the active rows before the by-package test. Kept.

S1: closed.
S2: closed.
S3: closed.
N1: closed.
N2: closed.
N3: closed.
N4: closed.
N5: kept.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N6 (nit) — #34346's acceptance names only the state with two enabled holders and a disabled binding. Its own Read section, and the jsdoc of `packagelessHolderRefusal`, also describe the draft save and delete with ONE enabled and one disabled holder (the disabled holder's row written or removed while the read serves the enabled one). CONTROL 2 of that card ("one enabled holder plus D's row unchanged") could be read as pinning it. Add the cell to the card's acceptance. Card text, not this tree.

N7 (nit) — the two no-row pins were pushed without a local run or an ablation (the PR body says so). CI on this head reads their TO; the FROM is by reading only. The pins also go through the protocol only, as the other delete pins do.

N8 (nit) — two unreleased notes of one release will contradict each other on the never-shipped-member save: `.changeset/33385-disabled-holders-env-404.md` line 19 says "accepted and kept, as before", and this changeset says it supersedes that line. The reader of the release notes gets both sentences. Correcting the older line is the cleaner end state, in this PR if the seat widens the file surface, or at release assembly.

N9 (nit) — two small residues by reading, neither pinned nor declared. (a) A bare no-row delete of an origin-gated code-defined item in these two states now answers this 409 before the origin-gated refusal that answered it; the changeset's refused-to-refused line names the save only. (b) The draft discard judges the draft rows alone, while the draft save judges the active rows and the drafts. With a package-unbound ACTIVE row the registry does not hold as the environment's item, and no draft, the draft save is left alone and the discard is refused where it answered the receipt. This is the same package-unbound class #34348 decides.
